scenario_A.description: Round 4 baseline - no Authority sign split
scenario_A.note: Authority_negative tokens counted alongside positive, inflating effective Authority

scenario_B.description: Round 5 revised - negative Authority reclassified as constraint/Nodality
scenario_B.note: Lower effective Authority -> lower IRR_intl -> larger Delta

key_evidence_quotes.quote: Emphasizes that the Belem Adaptation Indicators are voluntary, non-prescriptive, non-punitive, facilitative... shall not become a barrier and shall not be used under any circumstances as a condition for developing country Parties to access funding under the Convention and the Paris Agreement.
Also emphasizes that the Belem Adaptation Indicators do not create new financial obligations or commitments, nor liability or compensation.

Affirms that the Belem Adaptation Indicators... shall not create new obligations for developing country Parties, benchmarks or evaluation criteria, nor establish global standardized methodologies or data-collection processes, nor establish any compliance frameworks.
Emphasizes that no single adaptation approach shall be presented as the default, superior or universally applicable pathway.

interpretation.scenario_B_meaning: When negative Authority (shall NOT constraints) are reclassified as Nodality/constraint language rather than binding obligations, IRR_intl drops from 0.445 to 0.410, increasing Delta to 0.304.
interpretation.theoretical_implication: Para 7 and 9 of L.25E represent a deliberate strategy by Brazil (as COP30 chair) to protect G77 sovereignty by embedding negative obligations alongside voluntary Nodality language - a dual rhetorical device that simultaneously signals ambition (adopting indicators) and restraint (shall NOT create new obligations).
